subject.title: [Bug]: read tool drops memory/ prefix in multi-agent setup, causing ENOENT

question: Should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96453 be accepted as the canonical fix for this issue's bare daily-memory filename reads, or should maintainers require the prefix loss to be fixed upstream before the read tool?
rationale: Current main still lacks the behavior, and the open PR has focused proof but intentionally changes a read-tool fallback and sandbox validation path that ClawSweeper should not decide silently.

options.title: Accept the scoped read fallback
options.body: Land the open PR if maintainers agree that ENOENT-only bare date reads should resolve to canonical daily memory files while preserving sandbox validation.

options.title: Move the fix upstream
options.body: Ask for a replacement fix in the startup or prompt path that prevents the model from producing bare daily-memory filenames instead of teaching `read` a new fallback.

options.title: Hold for more live Windows proof
options.body: Keep the issue open and request a fresh Windows secondary-agent heartbeat or inbound-message trace before choosing the fix boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept the scoped read fallback
recommendation.body: Land the open PR if maintainers agree that ENOENT-only bare date reads should resolve to canonical daily memory files while preserving sandbox validation.

likelyOwner.reason: The open candidate PR changes the agent read-wrapper boundary, where this person has the strongest recent history signal.
